full_judgment:
2. The case for the petitioner, Managing Director, Dienfa Motors Ltd, 122/124, Motijheel Commercial Area, Dacca-2 is that-on the basis of a lease agreement for 30 years entered into with the Manager, Court of Wards, Dacca representing the heirs of Dacca Nawab Estate in 1951, the petitioner occupied the disputed premises on the terms and conditions as stated in the lease agreement (Annexure "A" to the petition) By order dated 6-7-77 (Annexure 'B' of the petition) the Respondent No. 1 Authorised Officer and Additional Land Acquisition Officer, Dacca issued notice under Section 3 of the Emergency Requisition of Property Act, 1948 requisitioning the premises occupied by the petitioner. Thereafter, the Respondent No. 1 issued the notice dated 11-7-77 (Annexure C to the petition) asking him to collect a sum of Tk. 7,50,000 as Advance and part payment of compensation for the requisition of the property as a person interested. The petitioner submitted a written representation to the Respondent No. 1 on 22-8-77 contending that full conversation having neither been assessed nor being offered the order of requisition is contrary to Section 5B of the said Act and, as such, void. In spite of the aforesaid protest made on 22-8-77 as per Annexure 'D' to the petition the Respondent No. 1 kept insisting upon the petitioner to hand ever vacant possession although full compensation is yet to be assessed by the respondents Till the filing of this petition the petitioner has received only a sum of 7k. 19,00,000 as against their claim for Tk. 68,00,000 on representations to the higher authority the time was extended on a few occasions. Ultimately on the expiry of the extended time the Additional Deputy Commissioner issued the following notice upon the petitioner on 18-8-78. 

 3. The Respondents entered appearance and filed affidavit-in-opposition. Their case is that after due verification on the spot and proper measurement with the help of expert Engineer (Executive Engineer PWD) the requisitioning authority reassessed the valuation of the building and structures at Tk. 28,81,067 against earlier assessment of Tk. 15,31,726,70 done by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Land Acquisition) Dacca. Out of the reassessed amount of Tk. 28,81,067 the petitioner has already received an amount of Taka 19,46,273. The balance amount, of Tk. 9,34,794 could not be paid due to failure on the part of the company to produce Income Tax clearance certificate and also due to objection petition filed by the General Manager, Nawab Estate, Court of Wards against four items of structures assessed. A miscellaneous case has already been started between the contending parties and the same is pending for disposal. There is no basis for the claim of the petitioner for a compensation of Tk. 68,00,000 The petitioner took lease for 30 years with effect from 1st October, 1947 and the period expired on 2nd October, 1977 and the petitioners are simply unauthorised possessors as they did not get lease renewed afresh from the Court of Wards. So the petition under Article 102 of the Constitution is not maintainable. Though the deed of lease was registered on 10-11-51 but it was acted upon with effect from 1st October, 1947. The notice of requisition dated 6-7-77 issued by the Additional Land Acquisition Officer was a valid notice as he was competent as an authorised officer under Section 2(1) of the said Act XIII of 1948 to issue such notice. Specific schedule of lands have also been given in the said notice. So the notice cannot be said to be vague. As per provision of Section 5B of the said Act 100% compensation money for structures and buildings was duly offered but due to objection of Court of Wards only for certain items payment offered could not be made on 22-8-77. However, on 17-678 after fresh assessment the petitioner company received full compensation money for their structures and buildings amounting to Tk. 19,46,27 which is 100% compensation for their undisputed structures and buildings. The petitioner, therefore, has no valid ground for challenge the legality of the requisition. On the prayer of the Dienfa Motors Ltd. (petitioner) time was allowed on various occasions to make over vacant possession. Lastly, on the expiry of the extended time the Additional Deputy Commissioner by his order dated 18-8-78 validly asked the petitioners to make over vacant possession on 19-8-78. The impugned order has been validity made. The disputed land in question was requisitioned for extension of Bangobhaban, which is the office-cum-residence of the President of Bangladesh. The said purpose of requisition is for public purpose and in the interest of public. The present petition is not maintainable as the petitioner did not file any appeal provided under the Act and also because they accepted the provisional compensation money. 

 12. Regarding the non-compliance with the provisions of Section 5B of the said Act it may be pointed out that the law requires that the petitioner is entitled to an offer of 100% compensation money for structures and buildings on the basis of a provisional estimate prepared on rough and ready calculation. In the present case the original provisional estimate for the structures and buildings was assessed at Tk. 7,51,000 and offered, excluding four items of the Structures of the Court of Wards as Court of Ward made objection. Therefore, the notice of advance payment of the said amount was quite justified. On the basis of fresh verification on the spot and proper measurement of machineries the requisitioning authority with the help of an expert. Engineer re-assessed the valuation of the buildings and structures, offered and paid Tk. 19,46,273 to the petitioner and the balance amount of Tk. 9,34,790 could not be paid due to the failure on the part of the petitioner to produce Income-Tax clearance certificate and also-due to the objection petition filed by the Chief Manager, Nawab Court of Wards against four items of structures assessed. A miscellaneous case has also been starts in respect of the claim regarding the compensation for four structures between the contesting parties and the same is pending for disposal. The petitioner's claim of Taka 68,00,000 as compensation money does not come within the purview of section 5(B) of the Act as the Deputy Commissioner is to offer the compensation on the basis of a provisional estimate prepared on rough and ready calculation.
